## D017 — `DeprecatedSdkExtra` {#d017}

**Tier:** `warn` · **Scope:** `app` · **Fix belongs in:** `packaging` · **Category:** `dependency-pinning` · **Autofixable:** yes · **Since:** 0.55.0

> Reference to a deprecated atlan-application-sdk shim extra removed in v4.0.0

**Rationale:** Seven SDK extras are shims: [workflows], [storage], [iam_auth] and [azure] list only
packages that are core, and [daft], [sqlalchemy] and [pandas] are [sql] or a subset of
it. They install nothing of their own and are removed in SDK v4.0.0. D017 applies when
the SDK requirement can resolve that release or later; a requirement capped below v4
cannot lose the extra under its current range. An extra is resolved by the installer,
not imported, so the SDK has no runtime deprecation warning to give: without this rule
an app learns of the removal only when it widens its SDK range for the v4 bump. Dropping
an extra changes nothing for the app today. Once the range admits a release where the
extra is gone, uv ignores the unknown extra and the app silently loses whatever it
pulled in. For [pandas] and [sqlalchemy] that is a missing package at runtime, so the
move to [sql] has to happen before that range is widened.

### What correct looks like

- **Compliant example:** atlan-openapi-app pyproject.toml — `atlan-application-sdk>=3.29.0,<4.0.0` in
  [project.dependencies], with no extras: everything it needs is core. An app that runs
  SQL names `[sql]`, and nothing else from the deprecated set.
- **Fix by:** [`programs/areas/dependency.prose.md`](https://github.com/atlanhq/application-sdk/blob/main/packages/conformance/conformance/programs/areas/dependency.prose.md)

An `atlan-application-sdk[extra]` reference whose version specifier admits SDK **v4.0.0
or later** names a deprecated shim extra. Each one installs nothing that the SDK's core
dependencies or `[sql]` do not already provide:

* `workflows`, `storage`, `iam_auth`/`iam-auth`, `azure`: the packages are core. Remove
  the extra.
* `daft`, `sqlalchemy`, `pandas`: `[daft]` is an alias for `[sql]` and the other two are
  subsets of it. Replace the extra with `sql` (drop it if `sql` is already listed).

A requirement capped below v4 cannot select a release where the extra has been removed,
so it is not flagged until the SDK range is widened.

::

    "atlan-application-sdk[iam-auth,pandas,sql,workflows]>=3.33,<5"  # flagged x3
"atlan-application-sdk[sql]>=3.33,<5"                             # passes
"atlan-application-sdk[pandas]>=3.33,<4"                          # passes: v4 excluded

Every array that can carry the SDK is checked: `[project] dependencies`,
`[project.optional-dependencies]` and `[dependency-groups]`, in either TOML string
quoting. `[incremental]` is not a shim: it is a supported alias for `[sql]` and is not
flagged.

Autofixable: rewrite the extras list as above when the SDK range admits v4 or later,
then re-run `uv lock` and review the lock diff. Dropping a core shim changes only the
lock's metadata. Replacing `[pandas]` or `[sqlalchemy]` with `[sql]` keeps every package
the shim installed but can add others (`[pandas]` alone gains `sqlalchemy` and `duckdb`;
`[sqlalchemy]` alone gains `pandas`, `pyarrow` and `duckdb`).

The rule carries `superseded_by: sdk>=4.0.0`: once v4 deletes the extras, a leftover
reference is an unknown extra, which D005 blocks. Cite: FND-4255.
